page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The processor includes 33 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for vector extensions including AVX and AVX-512F, along with AES cryptographic instructions. System memory totals 64.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes without bundled local storage and features a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with zero integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight the architectural profile of the underlying Broadwell-era processor. Single-core performance falls into lower percentiles, characterized by a Geekbench single-core score of 963.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 19.02 GB/sec. Conversely, the 32 dedicated threads deliver mid-tier multi-threaded throughput across diverse benchmarks, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,384.0 and a PassMark CPU rating of 23,057.96. Memory subsystem testing shows large-block uncached read speeds of 92.61 GB/sec and write speeds of 43.13 GB/sec. In application-focused metrics, the system managed 23.22 million Redis SET operations per second and 13.98 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From an infrastructure perspective, ecs.sn1ne.8xlarge trades peak single-thread execution speeds for consistent multi-core capacity across 32 threads. Because the instance lacks bundled ephemeral disks, primary storage operations depend entirely on remote block storage, impacting workloads requiring extreme local disk IOPS. The instance offers practical cost efficiency for horizontal, thread-parallel workloads that require dedicated CPU allocations without demanding excessive memory capacity per core. Recommended workloads include multi-threaded compilation tasks, distributed web serving, batch data processing, and microservice backends that fit comfortably within 64 GB of system memory.
